posts.hook: Your website has about 3 seconds to prove it's worth waiting for.
posts.why: 53% of mobile visitors leave a site that takes longer than 3 seconds to load. Not annoyed. Gone.
steps: Open your site on your phone using cellular data, not WiFi. Count to 3.
Run your homepage through Google's free PageSpeed Insights. Read the mobile results first.
Shrink any photo over 1 MB with a free tool like TinyPNG. Nobody will see the difference.
posts.take: A faster site keeps the people you already paid to attract.

captions.facebook:
Your website has about 3 seconds to prove it's worth waiting for.

Google's research found 53% of mobile visitors leave a site that takes longer than 3 seconds to load. Not "get annoyed." Leave.

3 things you can do today.
1. Open your site on your phone using cellular data, not WiFi, and count to 3. If it's not ready, you have a speed problem.
2. Run your homepage through Google's free PageSpeed Insights and read the mobile results first.
3. Check your biggest photos. Anything over 1 MB can usually be shrunk with a free tool like TinyPNG without looking any different.

A faster site means more of the people you already paid to attract actually stick around.

posts.hook: 97% of people read reviews before they pick a local business.
posts.why: And 41% now say they always read them before choosing, up from 29% the year before.
steps: Google your business and read your last 10 reviews the way a stranger would.
Check the date of your newest review. Over a month old? You need a steadier flow.
Ask every customer you finish a job for this week to leave a review.
posts.take: They will read your reviews. The question is whether you have enough recent ones to win them over.

captions.facebook:
97% of consumers read reviews for local businesses (BrightLocal, 2026). And 41% now say they "always" read them before choosing, up from 29% the year before.

Your reviews aren't a nice extra. For almost everyone deciding whether to call you, they're part of the decision.

3 things you can do today.
1. Google your business and read your last 10 reviews the way a stranger would.
2. Check the date of your most recent review. If it's more than a month old, you need a steadier flow.
3. Ask every customer you finish a job for this week to leave a review.

The question isn't whether people read your reviews. It's whether you'll have enough recent ones to win them over.

posts.hook: How does Google decide who shows up for “plumber near me”?
posts.why: Relevance, distance, and prominence. You can't move closer to every customer. You can improve the other two.
steps: Make sure your Google Business Profile lists every service you actually offer.
Ask your three most recent happy customers for a Google review.
Get listed on your local chamber of commerce site. It's a real, local link back to you.
posts.take: Relevance and prominence are in your control. Start there.

captions.facebook:
Ever wonder how Google decides which businesses show up for "plumber near me"?

Google says local results come down to three things, relevance (how well you match the search), distance (how close you are), and prominence (how well known you are, including your reviews and the websites that link to you). You can't move closer to every customer, but you can improve the other two.

3 things you can do today.
1. Make sure your Google Business Profile lists every service you actually offer.
2. Ask your three most recent happy customers for a Google review.
3. Get listed on your local chamber of commerce website. It's a real, local link back to your site.

Relevance and prominence are in your control. Start there.

posts.hook: Most calls to small businesses never reach a person.
posts.why: A study called 85 small businesses in 58 industries. Only 37.8% of calls were answered by a live human.
steps: Call your own business from another phone at a busy time. See what happens.
Listen to your voicemail greeting. Does it tell people when they'll hear back?
Count last week's missed calls that never got a callback.
posts.take: Every unanswered call is a customer deciding for you that you were too busy.

captions.facebook:
A 2024 study by 411 Locals called 85 small businesses across 58 industries. Only 37.8% of calls were answered by a live person. The rest went to voicemail or got nothing.

People calling a local service business usually have a problem right now. They don't want to wait. They want the next number on the list.

3 things you can do today.
1. Call your own business from a different phone at a busy time and see what happens.
2. Listen to your voicemail greeting. Does it tell people when they'll hear back?
3. Check your missed call log from last week and count how many never got a callback.

Every unanswered call is a customer deciding for you that you were too busy.

posts.hook: Your next customer might ask ChatGPT about you instead of Google.
posts.why: AI tools jumped from 6% to 45% of people using them to find local businesses, in a single year.
steps: Ask ChatGPT who the best [your type of business] in [your town] are.
Ask the same question in Google's AI Mode or Perplexity.
Write down who shows up. If it's your competitors, study their Google profiles and reviews.
posts.take: You can't fix what you haven't checked.

captions.facebook:
Your next customer might never type your name into Google. They might ask ChatGPT instead.

BrightLocal's 2026 survey found AI tools jumped from 6% to 45% of consumers using them to find local businesses in a single year. 31% had used ChatGPT for business recommendations. Google is still the biggest channel, but there's a new front door.

3 things you can do today.
1. Ask ChatGPT, "Who are the best [your type of business] in [your town]?"
2. Ask the same question in Google's AI Mode or Perplexity.
3. Write down who shows up. If it's your competitors and not you, look at their Google profiles and reviews. That's usually why.

You can't fix what you haven't checked.

posts.why: A CRM is one organized place for every lead and customer. Without one, it all lives in texts, sticky notes, and somebody's memory. And memories go on vacation.
steps: Count how many places customer info lives in your business right now.
Pick one place to be the single source of truth. A shared spreadsheet counts.
Put this week's new leads in that one place, and nowhere else.
posts.take: One place for every customer means nobody falls through the cracks.

captions.facebook:
“Did anyone call that lady back?” If you've ever asked that, this one's for you.

CRM stands for customer relationship management. In plain English, it's one organized place for every lead and customer you've ever had, including who called, what they needed, what you quoted, and when to follow up.

Without one, that information lives in texts, sticky notes, three inboxes, and somebody's memory. And memories go on vacation.

3 things you can do today.
1. Count how many places customer info lives in your business right now.
2. Pick one place to be the "single source of truth," even if it's a shared spreadsheet for now.
3. Move this week's new leads into it, and nowhere else.

One place for every customer means nobody falls through the cracks.

posts.hook: Those ads at the very top of Google with a badge and stars? Here's how they work.
posts.why: They're Local Services Ads. You pay per lead, not per click, and they show above regular ads and the map. Since October 2025 the badge says “Google Verified.”
steps: Search your main service in your town and note which competitors run these ads.
Check whether your business type is eligible on Google's Local Services Ads site.
Gather what verification usually asks for, like your license, insurance, and business details.
posts.take: Being ready is half the setup.

captions.facebook:
Ever notice the ads at the very top of Google for plumbers, electricians, and locksmiths, with a badge and a star rating? Those are Google Local Services Ads.

You pay per lead, like a call or message, not per click, and they show above regular ads and the map. One recent change. In October 2025, Google replaced the old "Google Guaranteed" and "Google Screened" badges with a single "Google Verified" badge, and the old money back guarantee ended.

3 things you can do today.
1. Search for your main service in your town and see which competitors have these ads.
2. Check whether your business type is eligible on Google's Local Services Ads site.
3. Gather what verification usually asks for, like your license, insurance, and business details.

Being ready is half the setup.
